Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Texas & Pacific Railway Company and its subsidiaries, including the Fort Worth Belt Railway Company and the Texas Pacific-Missouri Pacific Terminal Railroad of New Orleans, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Texas & Pacific Railway Company or its subsidiaries, including the Fort Worth Belt Railway Company and the Texas Pacific-Missouri Pacific Terminal Railroad of New Orleans, or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10109 describes creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10109_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10109_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_7785af79da.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated Dallas, Tex., March 9, 1950 (the letter of transmittal line reads 1960 in the text layer, an evident recognition error because the board was created on February 10, 1950). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking March 9, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on March 9, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to April 8, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event.
